terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Fitted, not guessed. Two independent estimates were made first - two-vanishing-point orthogonality on the apron's bottom edge and the pad's lower edge (f ~1390 px on a 1254 px square frame, i.e. ~48 deg vertical field), and a plane homography on the four foot positions (yaw -40.6 deg, rms 9.4 px) - and then 192 camera candidates were rendered and scored by align-then-IoU against the reference silhouette (tools/align_iou.py: both masks normalised to their own bounding box first, because raw IoU between a photograph and a procedural render is dominated by framing rather than fidelity). Best candidate yaw -40 deg, camera height 0.70 m, distance 1.413 m, vertical field 46 deg, target (0, 0.44, 0), aligned silhouette IoU 0.840 at blockout. A third estimate from the ratio of the projected front rail to the projected side rail gave 32 deg; it is the weakest of the three because it assumes the apron's plan proportions, which are themselves inferred.

objectClass.primaryType: side chair (armless dining/writing chair), ocean-liner interior c.1934
objectClass.notes: Four-legged armless side chair. Three material families in four named regions: pale figured sycamore veneer (back shell, seat apron and its bullnose lipping), macassar ebony (four round tapered legs, two of which continue upward as raked back stiles), deep-blue wool pad, chrome foot ferrules. Bilateral symmetry about the sagittal plane; one lofted concave surface (the back shell) and one open negative space (the reveal slot between shell and pad).

reasoning: Silhouette 2/3: rectilinear overall, but interrupted by the open reveal slot between back shell and seat pad and by four tapered round legs that read as separate strokes against the ground.
Component count 2/3: three macro assemblies (back, seat, undercarriage) resolving to eight meso parts and four micro feature groups; not a single body.
Material layers 2/3: four distinct PBR responses (satin sycamore veneer, satin macassar ebony with strong linear streak, matte wool, polished chrome) each occupying a named region.
Local detail density 2/3: rolled top edge on the back shell, bullnose lipping round the apron, the rounded pad edge, chrome ferrules with a shoulder, ebony streak figure, sycamore mottle figure.
Occlusion risk 2/3: the single three-quarter view hides the rear face of the back shell, the seat underside, the rear apron rail and the far rear foot.
Action readiness 1/3: static prop for a first-person walk; only a root transform is required, but every part must remain individually addressable (explodable/clickable).

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate: eight meso parts over three macro assemblies with four material layers and four micro feature groups. Repetition is real but shallow (the four legs and four ferrules are one mirrored/rotated system). Local overrides are required because the ebony streak runs along the leg axis while the sycamore mottle does not, and because the ferrule is the only metal in the model.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Rolled (half-round) top edge on the back shell, radius ~0.009 m, catching a continuous specular highlight along the whole top arc.
Back shell is a lofted concave surface, sagitta ~0.030 m over a 0.444 m chord, concave toward the sitter; its side edges are rounded full-round, not square.
Open reveal slot ~0.085 m tall between the bottom edge of the back shell and the top of the seat pad; the two ebony stiles are the only things crossing it.
Bullnose lipping roll, radius ~0.014 m, running the whole apron perimeter at its top edge; the pale band that frames the blue pad.
Apron plan corners are rounded, radius ~0.032 m, so the seat frame reads as a rounded-corner slab and not a box.
Wool pad has a rounded top edge (roll radius ~0.014 m) meeting the pale lipping with no welt or piping line; the top face is very slightly crowned.
Legs are circular in section, not square: radius falls linearly from ~0.0265 m under the apron to ~0.0110 m at the ferrule, with a very slight concave bow.
Polished chrome ferrule capping each foot: ~0.026 m tall, ~0.0112 m radius at its shoulder, tapering slightly with a rounded bottom rim; the only metal in the model.
Macassar ebony streak figure: near-black ground with warm reddish-brown stripes running along the leg axis, high contrast, sharp-edged, no relief.
Figured sycamore mottle: low-contrast irregular blotch figure over a warm pale tan ground, roughly isotropic, satin lacquer over it, no relief.
Fine woven wool micro-texture on the pad: matte, roughness ~0.92, no specular lobe, slight value noise only.
Rear legs carry a sabre knee just under the apron: the member is furthest forward at ~0.33 m, rakes back ~0.05 m to the foot and leans back again ~0.02 m to the stile top.

definitionOfDone: Silhouette from the reference three-quarter camera matches on: overall 0.88 m height, the reveal slot between back shell and pad, the reclined concave back shell with its rolled top edge, four round tapered legs with the rear pair raked, and chrome ferrules at all four feet.
The pale lipping band reads as an unbroken frame around the blue pad on every visible side.
Four material responses are distinguishable at the review camera: satin pale sycamore, near-black streaked macassar ebony, matte deep-blue wool, polished chrome.
Model holds up from at least three viewpoints (reference three-quarter, side, rear-quarter) with no interior gap, no floating part and no part intersecting the floor plane.
Triangle count under the real-time budget (target 6000) with no textures or external art; local origin at the centre of the footprint on the floor plane, front facing +z, real metres.

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

sculptPipeline.passOrderRationale: Five passes, not the eight-pass default. surface-pass is folded into material-pass because the reference carries no relief anywhere: veneer, lacquer and wool are all flat, and every figure is albedo-only. lighting-pass is dropped because this prop is lit by the holo-emitter scene it is dropped into, not by a rig it ships with; the review rig exists only to make the comparison fair. interaction-pass is folded into optimization-pass because the chair is static: it needs an explodable/clickable hierarchy and a collider proxy, and no pivots beyond the root.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
materialPass.texturelessRoute: All four materials declare textureless with evidence. This build emits no map of any kind: the factory imports only 'three', creates no canvas, loads no image, and every surface is a solid measured albedo with measured roughness/metalness/clearcoat/sheen. Surface figure is recorded in each material's localOverrides so it is not lost, and is recoverable by removing the textureless declaration and regenerating.

mustAvoid: reference lighting copied without separating material readability

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Declared real dimensions (0.88 x 0.46 x 0.50 m) are authoritative; measured pixel ratios were scaled onto them rather than the other way round.

The back is a single bent shell, not a panel in a frame: no joint line, shadow or break appears at the panel edge in the reference.
The chair is a machine-made cabinet piece, so the four legs carry no random variation.

componentTree.name: Back shell (lofted concave sycamore panel)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single bent-laminate panel: one continuous surface of constant thickness whose horizontal section is a circular arc and whose vertical section is straight. Extruding that measured arc band along the panel's own (reclined) axis reproduces it exactly; a box would lose the concavity that is the chair's first identity feature, and a continuous-sculpt/implicit route would spend triangles on a form that is genuinely developable.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser prop for a first-person walk: hold the triangle budget by choosing segment counts per component rather than by decimating measured curves. No textures at all - every material is a solid albedo plus procedural variation, so the draw-call count is the material count.

lightingFromPhoto: Key: high and camera-left-of-subject, roughly 35 deg above the horizon, soft-edged - the shell's top roll and the pad crown carry the brightest values and shadows under the apron are diffuse.
Fill: broad and cool from camera-right at roughly a quarter of the key, keeping the ebony readable instead of crushing it to black.
Rim/environment: a low neutral bounce off the flat rgb(128,128,128) ground, visible as the bright lower rim on each chrome ferrule.
Contact shadow: none in the reference - the chair floats on a flat grey field with no ground plane, so the review rig adds a soft contact shadow only to judge foot placement, never to score fidelity.
Exposure/tone mapping: mid-grey background sits at sRGB 128, so the review rig uses neutral exposure and ACES-free linear-to-sRGB output to keep the albedo comparison honest.
proceduralStrategy: Extrude every measured plan outline (shell arc band, apron, pad) rather than approximating it with a box, so the plan curvature that identifies the chair is exact.
Sweep every rolled edge as a tube on its own path so the roll radius stays constant through the rounded plan corners.
Sweep both leg families as tapered sweeps on measured spines: the front pair straight, the rear pair on the sabre spine that also carries the stile.
Lathe the ferrules: they are turned parts and a surface of revolution is their exact description.
Keep every material a solid albedo plus a procedural variation field with a fixed seed. No image files, no canvas bitmaps, no external art.
Bake nothing about the reference's own lighting into albedo: the prop is relit by the scene.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-object translate/rotate/scale and visibility for scene placement
each leg pivot sits at its apron socket, so a leg can be detached or swung without rebuilding geometry
the back-shell pivot sits at the shell's bottom-centre front face, on the recline axis, so the recline angle stays editable as a single rotation
destructionAnchors: fracture groups: back-assembly (shell + its roll), seat-assembly (apron, both apron rolls, pad, pad roll), undercarriage (four legs + four ferrules)
the leg sockets at the apron corners are the plausible break points; the shell's stile lap is the second
risks: Single view: the back recline is measured between 12 and 16 degrees depending on how much of the silhouette shift is attributed to perspective. Modelled at 12 degrees to keep overall depth inside the declared 0.50 m; if a rear view ever arrives this is the first number to re-measure.
The rear-leg rake and the sabre knee are read from a single three-quarter view where the far rear leg is partly occluded; the near rear leg carried most of the measurement.
Procedural wood figure cannot reproduce the specific bird's-eye mottle of the reference veneer; it reproduces its statistics (contrast, scale, isotropy) only. Stated as an approximation, not a match.
